audit_findings.title: The gross cash add-back may include cash unavailable to current common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,129.6 million identified claims ($457.7 million client-funds shortfall plus $671.9 million dividend payable), equal to $2.79 per diluted share and 26.7% of the $4,230.1 million cash add-back
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces the cash bridge added to equity value; it does not alter owner earnings or growth.
audit_findings.evidence: For client funds liquidity, we have the ability to borrow through our financing arrangements under our U.S. short-term commercial paper program and our U.S., Canadian and United Kingdom short-term reverse repurchase agreements ($7.5 billion of which is available on a committed basis in the U.S. as of June 30, 2026) , together with our $11.7 billion of comm itted credit facilities and our ability to use corporate liquidity when necessary to meet short-term funding requirements related to client funds obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed balance sheet demonstrates that funds held for clients were $457.7 million below client-funds obligations and that a $671.9 million declared dividend was payable. Deducting both identified claims would reduce each scenario by $2.79 per share: bear to about $127.67, base to $184.32, and bull to $204.72. This cannot close the $76.02 gap between the $283.53 market price and the existing $207.51 bull value, so it does not change the valuation conclusion. Whether additional corporate cash was committed between June 30 and September 4 remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Roll corporate cash and liabilities from June 30 to September 4, classify the client-funds shortfall and dividend payment, test for duplication in working-capital adjustments, and rerun the bridge with only cash demonstrably available to September 4 common equity.

audit_findings.title: Client-float earnings may not support the same growth rate as service owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,354.8 million of fiscal-2026 client-funds interest revenue, equal to 33.1% of the $4,087.2 million OE anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes the OE anchor if integral float earnings were purged, and changes forecast growth and terminal value if retained float earnings were grown at service-business rates.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in interest earned on funds held for clients resulted from an increase in our average client funds balances of 7.4% to $40.4 billion in fiscal 2026 as compared to fiscal 2025, coupled with an increase in our average interest rate earned to 3.4% in fiscal 2026, as compared to 3.2% in fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved but material modeling issue. The filing establishes that client-funds interest is an operating revenue stream driven by $40.4 billion of average client balances and a 3.4% earned rate, but the record does not show what the stated portfolio-interest purge removed or the associated funding costs and taxes. Purging integral float earnings would understate value; retaining them while applying undifferentiated 7% or 9% growth could overstate value. At 33.1% of the OE anchor on a gross-revenue comparison, the component is reasonably capable of changing the valuation range or conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE calculation to the $371.0 million corporate interest income and $1,354.8 million client-funds interest separately, then rerun all scenarios with client-float net earnings forecast from client-balance growth, portfolio repricing, realized losses, funding costs, and taxes.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized contract-acquisition and implementation costs may be missing from reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $107.4 million pretax net investment ($1,307.9 million additions less $1,200.5 million amortization), equal to 2.63% of the $4,087.2 million anchor; if wholly omitted, approximately $4.64 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring cash additions to deferred contract costs must replace GAAP amortization in OE reinvestment; omission overstates the OE anchor and all operating present values.
audit_findings.evidence: Incremental costs of obtaining a contract (e.g., sales commissions) that are expected to be recovered are capitalized and amortized on a straight-line basis over a period of three to eight years , depending on the business unit.
audit_findings.explanation: The $107.4 million net cash investment is demonstrated by the filing, but whether the OE calculation omitted it is unresolved because the anchor build is not supplied. At fixed base-case assumptions, a complete $107.4 million anchor overstatement would reduce base operating value by approximately $1,880 million, or $4.64 per share, leaving base value near $182.47 and still far below the $283.53 price. Thus even the full identified omission would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce the line-by-line 2026 OE reconciliation and confirm that the $1,200.5 million amortization was added back only alongside deduction of the $1,307.9 million cash additions; if absent, reduce the anchor by $107.4 million and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The business-alignment add-back could strip a recurring cash cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $91.1 million pretax and $67.9 million after tax, equal to 1.66% of the $4,087.2 million anchor after tax; if fully added back, approximately $2.93 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: An adjusted-earnings add-back would increase the OE anchor; alternatively, any unpaid amount could reduce the equity bridge if the expense was excluded from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Severance charges have been taken in the past and not included as an adjustment to get to adjusted results.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $91.1 million charge and a $23.2 million associated tax benefit, but the record does not establish that the valuation added back the resulting $67.9 million after-tax cost. If it did, reversing the full add-back would reduce base operating value by approximately $1,189 million, or $2.93 per share, leaving base value near $184.18 and not changing the conclusion relative to the $283.53 price. Future restructuring recurrence is presently unquantified, but the identified current-period amount is not material to the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to GAAP versus adjusted net earnings and the business-alignment adjustment; if the $67.9 million after-tax charge was added back, remove it or substitute a documented normalized restructuring allowance, then rerun all scenarios and separately identify any unpaid liability.
